title: Civil Reconnaissance Sergeant (CR SGT) (Active Component Only)
raw_text:
10-38R. MOS 38R—Civil Reconnaissance Sergeant (CR SGT) (Active Component Only), CMF 38
(Eff 202410)
     a. Major duties. The Civil Reconnaissance Sergeant serves as the technical civil reconnaissance
expert of a regionally aligned four-person Civil Affairs Team (CAT). The Civil Reconnaissance Sergeant
employs reconnaissance efforts on a CAT in hostile, denied, or politically sensitive environments through
the utilization of specialized tactics, techniques, and procedures to conduct civil reconnaissance, civil
engagement, and civil network development to find, disrupt, and defeat threats in the civil component.
Duties of MOS 38BR at each level of skill are:
          (1) MOSC 38R1O. (Personnel Only). MOS used to identify Soldiers accessed into MOS 38R prior
to obtaining grade SSG.
          (2) MOSC 38R2O. (Personnel Only). MOS used to identify Soldiers accessed into MOS 38R prior
to obtaining grade SSG.
          (3) MOSC 38R3O. Provides reconnaissance, infrastructure assessment, language, and regional
expertise as part of a CAT. Conducts civil reconnaissance, performs civil engagements, assists in civil
network development and engagement, and supports Transitional Governance. The Civil
Reconnaissance Sergeant also integrates with supported organizations to identify requirements for Civil
Affairs Operations (CAO) and Civil Military Operations (CMO) that enables supported commanders the
ability to preserve combat power while consolidating gains across the competition continuum.
    b. Physical demands rating and qualification for initial award of MOS. Civil Reconnaissance Sergeant
must possess the following qualifications:
          (1) A physical demands rating of Significant (Gray).
          (2) A physical profile of 111221.
          (3) Qualifying scores.
              (a) A minimum score of 107 in aptitude area GT.
              (b) A minimum score of 100 in aptitude area CO.
          (4) A minimum OPAT score of Long Jump (LJ) – 0120 cm, Seated Power Throw (PT) – 0350 cm,
Strength Deadlift (SD) – 0120 lbs., and Interval Aerobic Run (IR) – 0036 shuttles in Physical Demand
Category “Significant” (Gray).
          (5) Must be airborne qualified and maintain SQI P Parachutist or volunteer to attend Basic
Airborne Course.
          (6) Must be Survival, Evasion, Resistance, and Escape Level C (SERE-C) graduate effective on
and after 1 October 2024.
          (7) A minimum security eligibility of SECRET is required for the initial award and to maintain the
MOS.
          (8) A U.S. citizen or naturalized citizen.
          (9) High school graduate or GED certificate.
          (10) Not barred to reenlist IAW AR 601-280, or under suspension of favorable personnel action
IAW AR 600-8-2.
          (11) No history of a qualifying military or civilian conviction of a crime of domestic violence, as
defined by AR 600-20, Army Command Policy, paragraph 4-22.
          (12) No history of any use of an illicit substance following the Soldier's date of initial entry into
military service.
          (13) No history of any use of a controlled substance without a valid prescription following the
Soldier's date of initial entry into military service.
          (14) No history of a military or civilian charge for Driving Under the Influence or Reckless Driving.
          (15) No history of any other open military or civilian administrative or criminal investigation,
charge, or indictment on the Soldier
          (16) No record of conviction by special or general courts-martial or civilian courts of offenses
listed in AR 27-10 (Military Justice) chapter 24 or otherwise required to register as a sexual offender
under AR 27-10, chapter 24.
          (17) Reclassification.
              (a) Active Component Soldiers: Must be in grade E4/SPC with Basic Leadership Course
  (BLC) completion and a minimum of 12 months of Active Federal Service through E6/SSG with no more
  than 10 years Active Federal Service (waivable by the CA Proponent) and must meet the prerequisites
  IAW AR 614-200 to include successful attendance and selection at the Civil Affairs Assessment and
  Selection Course (CAAS) (non-waivable).



                                                       1
               (b) Formal Training: Active Component Soldiers must successfully complete the Civil Affairs
Assessment and Selection Course (CAAS), Basic Airborne Course (if not already qualified), Survival,
Evasion, Resistance, and Escape Level C (SERE-C), Civil Reconnaissance Sergeant Phase I and Phase
II courses, Civil Affairs Sluss-Tiller Course, and Basic Special Operations Language Training, and Civil
Reconnaissance Sergeant Phase III Course conducted under the auspices of the U.S. Army John F.
Kennedy Special Warfare Center and School (USAJFKSWCS).
       (18) Accessions. Initial entry trainee must complete the 12B10-OSUT (Combat Engineer) course,
Civil Affairs Preparation and Conditioning Course, Civil Affairs Assessment and Selection Course (CAAS),
Basic Airborne Course, Basic Leader Course (BLC), Survival, Evasion, Resistance, and Escape Level C
(SERE-C), Civil Reconnaissance Sergeant Phase I and Phase II courses, Civil Affairs Sluss-Tiller Course,
Basic Special Operations Language Training, and Civil Reconnaissance Sergeant Phase III Course
conducted under the auspices of the U.S. Army John F. Kennedy Special Warfare Center and School
(USAJFKSWCS).
    c. Additional skill identifiers (ASIs): Refer to table 12-8 for listing of universal ASIs associated with all
enlisted MOSs.
      (1) 6B--Reconnaissance and Surveillance Leaders Course (personnel only).
      (2) 6H--Minimum MOS Qualified-Staff Sergeant (personnel only) (Effective 202408).
      (3) 7H--Minimum MOS Qualified-Sergeant First Class (personnel only) (Effective 202408).
    d. Physical requirements and Standards of Grade (SG). Physical requirements and SG relating to
each skill level are listed in the following tables:
        (1) Table 10-38R-1. Physical requirements.
        (2) Table 10-38R-2. Standards of grade TOE/MTOE.
        (3) Table 10-38R-3. Standards of grade TDA.

The Civil Reconnaissance Sergeant employs reconnaissance efforts on a CAT in hostile, denied, or politically sensitive environments through the utilization of specialized tactics, techniques, and procedures to conduct civil reconnaissance, civil engagement, and civil network development to find, disrupt, and defeat threats in the civil component.
Inspect buildings, fences, fields or ranges, supplies, and equipment to determine work to be performed.
Provides reconnaissance, infrastructure assessment, language, and regional expertise as part of a CAT.
Advise authorities of procedures to be followed in radiation incidents or hazards, and assist in civil defense planning.
Conducts civil reconnaissance, performs civil engagements, assists in civil network development and engagement, and supports Transitional Governance.
Coordinate with agencies, such as air traffic control, civil engineers, or command posts, to ensure support of airfield management activities.

The Civil Reconnaissance Sergeant also integrates with supported organizations to identify requirements for Civil Affairs Operations (CAO) and Civil Military Operations (CMO) that enables supported commanders the ability to preserve combat power while consolidating gains across the competition continuum.

nlx_method: NLx employer-demand profiles; private-only ownership unverified. Six-digit profiles pool specialty weighted task incidences after the existing review exclusion mask and five-job task-support floor; destination SOCs require 200 postings and nonzero tasks. Military profiles use binary accepted task presence and the same NLx reference RCA weights as civilian profiles: reciprocal positive task shares (zero weight for reference-absent tasks) of pooled retained support-five NLx weighted incidences across 1,016 reference specialties (912 eligible comparison candidates), sqrt(q * rca_weight), then L2 normalization and cosine. No military crosswalk codes enter the task ranking. All positive top-20 results retained; zero-similarity destinations are not recommendations. Shared field/rating duties are included; general Naval Standards remain separate by paygrade. Summary compares non-future individual source entries (versions can repeat) with nonempty reference sets; grouped, future and general-standard entries remain in all outputs. Hit@k is the fraction with at least one reference SOC recovered; ties are averaged exactly. References outside NLx remain in denominators. DMDC reference status is from July 2024, not current 2026 status.
